newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PIERCE BUNDLES FIFTH SEED HUBER OUT OF OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE BUNDLES FIFTH SEED HUBER OUT OF OPEN.

text.p: Former champion Mary Pierce of France became the first player to advance to the quarter-finals of the Australian Open on Sunday when she upset German fifth seed Anke Huber in straight sets.
Pierce, ranked 22 in the world and unseeded in Melbourne, controlled the match from the baseline downing Huber, an Open finalist last year, 6-2 6-3 in one hour and 23 minutes.
The Canadian-born right-hander, who celebrated her 22nd birthday last week, has been in superb touch over the past week dropping only one set in four matches.
The 1995 Australian Open champion served strongly and broke Huber's serve on three occasions in the opening set which lasted 33 minutes.
Huber, who reached her first Grand Slam final at the Australian Open last year before losing to Monica Seles, struggled with her serve, double-faulting five times.
Pierce will play either Spanish third seed Conchita Martinez or 16th seed Sabine Appelmans of Belgium in the quarter-finals. Martinez and Appelmans are due to meet each other later on Sunday.
